items.note: RCT in a three-day hackathon: 22 early-career social scientists randomized to unrestricted GPT-4 or no AI; experts scored manuscripts on six dimensions including originality (no effect on originality). Abstract from the Research Square version (same study as SSRN); below 50 participants.

Controlled experiment comparing divergent and convergent LLM personas with a standard direct-answer LLM (AI vs AI, no no-AI arm) on creative problem solving with objective creativity measures; abstract gives no N (search notes say 105 recruited, 101 analyzed, randomized).

Three-paper doctoral thesis; paper 2 runs three experiments comparing GenAI-assisted and human-only product ideation with novelty and appropriateness outcomes. Likely overlaps with Sabbah, Banerjee, Li (2026, c542); full text embargoed.

Four ideation configurations (human-only, unstructured GenAI collaboration, GenAI seeding, TC-based GenAI seeding) with 400 professionals; experts rate novelty, utility, feasibility. The AOM Proceedings version (10.5465/amproc.2026.48bp) reports n = 350 for the same study; likely overlaps with the Sabbah thesis (c541).

Within-subject study with 20 programmers, LLM-assisted vs unassisted; measures idea-generation time, creative moments, and number of ideas in solutions; order randomization not stated; below 50 participants.

Preregistered within-subject experiment: Japanese and American participants write workplace emails without AI, with a low-context AI draft, and with a high-context AI draft; outcome is cultural style markers (convergence toward the draft's style), which may count as a homogenization outcome. Abstract gives no N (search notes say 175, counterbalanced).

50 Palestinian educational-technology students randomly assigned to learn with GAI tools or traditional instruction; post-test on an 18-item creativity scale (fluency, flexibility, originality, elaboration) that may be a self-report scale; the abstract also calls the design quasi-experimental.
Indonesian quasi-experiment with 70 grade-10 students (35 Gemini-assisted math class, 35 control class); creative-thinking test N-gain higher with Gemini; abstract in Indonesian.

Pilot study: 30 novice designers ideate with traditional methods and with an LLM conversational ideation interface; an expert panel compares fluency, novelty, and variety qualitatively; mainly a system paper, below 50 participants.

Quasi-experiment with 186 undergraduates randomized at the department level to ChatGPT and Midjourney in digital story development or the same process without AI; outcomes are design-thinking mindset, creative self-efficacy, and reflective-thinking self-efficacy (all self-reports).
